newsitem.title: USA: No chair for Tony Blair at Denver summit.
newsitem.headline: No chair for Tony Blair at Denver summit.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair briefly found himself odd man out in a unplanned game of musical chairs at the Denver summit of big industrial powers on Saturday.

As summit leaders gathered for their first plenary session in a blue-carpeted conference room of the Denver Public Library, an aide from each delegation was supposed to move a padded high-backed chair from the outer perimeter of the room to a circular conference table.
But Blair's chair was missing, and his staff went scurrying for something for him to sit on.

The only thing immediately at hand was a smaller chair that left the British prime minister looking less distinguished than his summit partners -- the leaders of the United States, France, Italy, Germany, Japan, Canada and Russia.
Blair's real chair was finally located, but he made do with the substitute temporarily as proceedings were getting under way.
The diplomatic embarrassment led to wisecracks among officials and reporters that the old Anglo-American "special relationship" semed to have gone by the board.
Blair, who has close ties with summit host President Bill Clinton, had no comment on the snafu.
